newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SIMEON SAYS HAS 70 PCT OF AUSTVIN.
newsitem.headline: SIMEON SAYS HAS 70 PCT OF AUSTVIN.

text.p: Australian wine producer Simeon Wines Ltd said on Thursday it was now entitled to about 70 percent of shares in takeover target Australian Vintage Ltd.
"The directors of Austvin, who previousy held in aggregate 25.5 percent of the shares in Austvin, have now accepted the offer," managing director Neil MacKenzie said in a statement.
MacKenzie said Simeon had extended the offer period, due to close on August 15, to August 25 to allow shareholders who had not yet accepted the offer to do so.

Simeon originally offered in April four of its shares plus A$3.60 cash for every five AustVin shares, supplementing that in June with an alternative offer of one Simeon share plus A$3.16 cash for every two AustVin shares.
Simeon has said previously a successful merger would create Australia's fourth largest winemaker by volume.
Assets of a merged group would include:
- two wine processing facilities with capacity of 100,000 tonnes processing 12 percent of Australia's wine grape crop with access to fruit from Australia's largest grape growing regions.
- 3,000 acres of vineyards in the Padthaway, Cowra, Riverland and Sunraysia districts.
